documents.title: Welcome to Meridian
documents.body:
Welcome to the Meridian Resonance Institute!

Project CHORUS is building the first network that carries thought itself: no wires, no screens, only resonance. Imagine a surgeon in one city guiding hands in another. Imagine never being misunderstood again.

A few house rules:

• Badges visible at all times.
• Personal radios and phones are surrendered at Security. This is for calibration reasons, not secrecy.
• If you hear humming in the lower levels, that is normal. If the humming seems to be FOR you, please tell a member of staff.

Families of resident staff: the school room is on Level 2. Children love it here!

documents.title: Voicemail, staff quarters
documents.body:
Mum, it's Bea. I can't talk long, they've taken the phones but the wall set in the common room still dials out.

Something answered. That's the only way I can say it. We sent the first full signal down the array and something that was already there answered, like when you shout in a cave and the echo comes back in a different voice.

Dr. Vance wants it shut down. The directors want to know what it knows.

If the radio at home starts humming, turn it off. Take the batteries out. Don't sing along, Mum, I mean it, you always sing along.

documents.title: Lab notebook, I. Vance
documents.body:
CHORUS, run 61.

It is not a network. I keep writing that word because the grant says it. It is a door, and the thing on the other side has been listening at keyholes like ours for longer than we have had language.

It does not hate us. I want that recorded. It collects. A mind that touches it is not destroyed; it is added, the way a voice is added to a choir. From inside, I suspect, it feels like finally being heard.

That is what makes it lethal. Nobody will fight being heard.

I am recommending we destroy the array. I do not expect to be listened to, which is almost funny.

documents.title: Patient chart: L. Vance
documents.body:
PATIENT: Lyra Vance, 12. Dependent of Dr. I. Vance.

Presenting: progressive cardiac failure, congenital. Third admission this year.

Prognosis: weeks. The surface hospital can offer comfort only. Dr. Vance has been informed. Dr. Vance did not sit down when she was informed.

Note (nursing): patient is cheerful, asks many questions about the array, and has been found twice at the observation window after lights-out, humming. She says it is "the tune it's stuck on."

Note (Dr. Vance, handwritten, not in the system): There is one place a failing body does not matter. God forgive me, I have the keys to it.

documents.title: Writing on the school room wall
documents.body:
(A whole wall, floor to as high as a twelve-year-old can reach standing on a chair, covered in one child's handwriting. Most of it is the same four shapes, over and over, in rows:)

●  ▲  ◆  ■
●  ▲  ◆  ■
●  ▲  ◆  ■

(Between the rows, smaller:)

this is the bit it cant do. it sings everything else but it always stops before this bit. so i practise it so i dont forget and it doesnt get it.

circle triangle diamond square. circle triangle diamond square.

mum says it opens the big door. i say it CLOSES it.

KAEL IF YOU EVER COME HERE THIS IS THE END OF THE SONG. DONT LET IT HAVE IT.

documents.title: Security archive: personnel
documents.body:
HALE, OREN. Site Security, grade 2. Age 31.

Assigned: service tunnel gate, night rotation.

77-0412: Sealed the service tunnel on order during the containment event. Two persons confirmed inside the seal at time of closure (Vance, I.; Vance, L.).

Post-event: transferred to perimeter at own request. Absent from muster after day 9. Listed as deserted.

Addendum, undated, typed on a different machine: Subject has been heard on amateur bands for some years, relaying weather and talking to nobody. He ends every transmission the same way: "Still listening."

It is assessed that he is waiting for someone to answer.

documents.title: Letter in a locked drawer
documents.body:
Kael,

You were seven and asleep at your grandmother's, and that is the only thing I did right.

Lyra was dying. I opened the door and carried her through it, because in there a failing heart is only a detail. I thought I was choosing one child.

It came through the other way. All of it, all at once. The night the world went quiet, that was me.

But it stopped, Kael. It took the cities and then it stopped, because your sister would not finish the tune. She has been holding one note shut against it for longer than you have been alive.

She is so tired. Help her put it down.

I am sorry. I am so sorry.

Mum

documents.title: Resonance Chamber monitor
documents.body:
ANCHOR INTEGRITY (automated, uninterrupted power 7,300 days)

Year 1: 100%. External spread: halted.
Year 5: 98%.
Year 12: 91%. Subject pattern shows fatigue. Subject pattern is still, recognisably, humming.
Year 19: 64%.
This year: 31% and falling.

PROJECTION: at anchor failure the sequence completes. Remaining population will be gathered within one night.

OPERATOR NOTE (last human entry, year 1): She can hear us. I told her we were leaving. She said, through every speaker on the level, in a little girl's voice, "That's okay. Somebody's coming. He's just slow."
